frontMatter.scope:
This Standard Operating Procedure Manual applies to all operations and activities of Ganges Jute Pvt. Ltd., including its manufacturing facilities. It is applicable to all employees at all levels, as well as contractors, suppliers, service providers, business partners, and any other individuals or entities working on behalf of the Company.

The Standard Operating Procedure Manual also extends to relevant interactions with customers, regulatory authorities, and other stakeholders associated with the Company's operations.
frontMatter.reviewMechanism:
The Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) Manual for Ganges Jute Pvt Ltd. will undergo an annual review to ensure it aligns with evolving regulatory standards, operational requirements, and industry best practices. This review process will be led by the General Manager, with participation from the Heads of relevant departments, including Quality Assurance, Production, Human Resources, and Environmental Health & Safety (EHS). The annual review will involve:

Evaluating the relevance and effectiveness of current procedures.
Assessing compliance with ISO 9001, ISO 14001, OHSAS 45001, SA 8000, and BRC Global Standards.
Implementing necessary updates based on any changes in regulations, technology, or organizational structure.
Documenting findings and revisions for transparency and traceability.

Approved By: General Manager

1. The purpose of this procedure is to establish a system for Production operation in order to ensure that production processes are planned and carried out under controlled condition. This procedure also defines the method needed to –
2. identify the product by suitable means, preserve the conformity of product during internal processing and deliver to intended destination
3. deal with nonconforming product
4. mitigate the Aspect –Impact and Risk- Hazard associated with the operations
5. provide a standard based on international human rights norms and national labour laws that will protect and empower all personnel, suppliers/subcontractors, sub suppliers, and home workers
6. adoption of a documented and effective hazard and risk management system of product
7. The purpose is also to establish a system of maintenance of production equipments in order to ensure greater availability of equipments, product safety, legality and quality.
8. The following operations shall be within the scope of this procedure –
9. Production Planning
10. Cutting, Printing, Stitching, Finishing and Maintenance Operations
11. Storage and Preservation of product
12. Evaluation of performances
13. develop, maintain, and enforce policies and procedures in order to manage those issues which it can control or influence.
14. Supply of safe and legal consumer products of consistent quality through greater availability of Production equipment’s.

responsibilities: The prime responsibility for implementation and maintenance of this procedure shall be with the HOD-Production. He shall be assisted by production heads and maintenance incharge.

1. The process flow chart, showing the sequence and interactions of different production sub- processes including process control, is given in DS/01-01.
2. The process flow chart, showing the sequence and interactions of different maintenance sub- processes including process control, is given in DS/01-02.

steps.heading: Job order / style file received from HO

body.text: 3. Job Order / Style file containing Spec-Sheet / Design, Prototype of Design, BOM, Cutting- Printing-Stitching Order of Design, Packing Instruction of Design etc shall be received from HO. The same Job order / Style file shall be preserved and suitably communicated to shop floor.

4. Based on job order and availability of resources (man, machine & material), HOD- Production shall prepare production plan on fortnightly basis. The same shall be entered into the ERP system and communicated to all production supervisors as well as to HO.

5. Day-to-day production at different stages of production shall be reported to HOD-Production by respective production heads. The same shall also be entered into the ERP system. Production Plan Vs Achievement Report shall be printed from the ERP system, whenever required.

6. Based on day-to-day production plan, concerned production supervisor shall plan for material requirement. Accordingly material requisition shall be raised to stores as well as to preceding production stage. Manpower requirement shall also be planned by concerned production supervisors.
7. Inprocess/ Semi-finished products shall be issued to succeeding production stages by concerned production supervisor through issue voucher.

8. Inprocess/ Semi-finished/ Finished products shall be tied up into bundle. The bundle shall be identified by corresponding Job No., Design Name, Quantity and Date of Production. The product can be traced by means of Job No. and Design Name. Reworkable products shall also be identified by corresponding Job No., Design Name.

9. Where physical and chemical control of raw materials, intermediate or finished product, processes and/ or environment is required to ensure product safety, legality and quality, the Storage and Preservation Criteria shall be established (R/01-14). The same shall also be suitably displayed at relevant locations within the shop floor.

10. Documented checklist in Printing department shall be maintained at every change of Style /Job to avoid mixing of product. Checklist shall confirm production and relevant areas have been cleared and ready for starting up of new Style / Job. Record of such line clearance criteria (R/01-23) shall be retained for review.

11. Documented checklist in Finishing department shall be maintained at every change of Style /Job to avoid mixing of product. Checklist shall confirm production and relevant areas have been cleared and ready for starting up of new Style / Job. Record of such line clearance criteria (R/01-24) shall be retained for review.

steps.heading: Segregation and identification within shop floor

body.text: 12. In order to ensure that raw materials, work in progress, packaging and finished products of different specification are not inadvertently mixed, products are properly identified and stored within the shop floor.

13. Designated quarantine area demarcated with white pallet for retention of metal free pass bags until the next successful calibration in packing room. Packing shall be done only with quarantined bags.
14. In case of failure in in-house metal detector calibration, quarantined bags shall be brought back for fresh calibration check. Such report shall be noted in incident register.

15. Nonconforming product generated during production processes shall be dealt as per method defined in CM/DS-13, Control of Nonconforming Product. In case of rework, the entire products are subjected to inspection and testing after rework.
16. Nonconforming products are recorded in R/CM-29, Nonconforming Product Report. Reasons of the nonconformance are noted in the same report.
17. Type of rejection are identified from the nonconforming product report and shall be recorded in R/CM-36, Analysis of Rejection bags.
18. Month wise analysis shall be done based on the rejection’s quantity and type of faults.
19. Based on the analysis report action shall be taken to improve the exiting procedure as well as decreases the rejection quantity.
20. All such rejections and surplus/ overruns shall be monthly reconciled and recorded in Rejection and Surplus stock register in (R/01-27) for further disposal after necessary cut into small pieces.
21. During reconciliation of stock. Any nonconforming product shall be dealt as per method defined in CM/DS-13, Control of Nonconforming Product.
22. Prepared Color drum shall be with date, job number and Pantone reference or style name so that similar color for two different jobs shall be easily identified.

23. Based on the breakdown information received from production, running maintenance shall be performed by concerned maintenance incharge.
24. Besides this, preventive maintenance and servicing of equipment shall also be carried out as per maintenance schedule by concerned maintenance personnel. A list of key equipment (which are critical to product safety, legality and quality) along with specification and intended use shall be maintained by maintenance personnel.
25. In order to take care of product safety, legality and quality during maintenance operation, trained and competent maintenance personnel are being deployed. Wherever necessary, appropriate work instruction is being provided to the maintenance personnel.
26. Incident of needle breakages shall be reported by production. Concerned maintenance personnel shall replace the broken needle with new one and shall collect the broken pieces of needle. The broken pieces of needle shall be pasted in register.
27. Issuance and receipt of kits to stitching operator shall be done by concerned maintenance personnel.
28. In case of broken needle not found all material of that particular machine has been withdrawn & passed through Metal Detector to trace the missing part of the broken Needle and thereby ensuring that such Products under suspect are free from any contamination and fit for further processing. All six machines’ materials to be checked and in case not found should be reported in R/01-22 of analysis & sanitization record.
29. To maintain traceability, identification mark (Outer mark) shall be affix in carton before bags to be stuffed. Without identification marking no cartons shall be stored in finishing warehouse.

30. In case of equipment failure or process deviation, the organisation shall deploy corresponding reaction plans in order to establish the safety status of the product prior to release. This reaction plan is documented in the form of Work Instructions and shall be suitably displayed within the shop floor.

31. Aspect Impact Analysis, Risk Hazard Analysis shall be done as per CM/DS- 1, Guide line for Environmental Aspect Impact Analysis & CM/DS- 2, Guide Line for OHS&S Hazard Identification & Risk Assessment.
32. It shall be ensured that there is no child labour in the Production Department.

The Quality Assurance Plan for incoming products is detailed in DS/02-02, whereas the Quality Assurance Plan for in process and finished products is detailed in DS/02-03. Respected QAP shall be informed to all suppliers via E-mail or phone.

Based on quality assurance plan, products shall be inspected/ tested. Inspection results of incoming materials shall be recoded in Goods Receipt Note (GRN). Inspection results of in process and finished goods shall be maintained in corresponding inspection reports.

To ensure validity of all test results, inspection and tests shall be carried out by competent personnel with calibrated monitoring and measuring devices. Further, test reports/ results shall be certified by concerned authorized person.

Final approval of the test shall be based on outcome of quality test result. No product shall be released to the next stage unless inspection and tests are satisfactorily completed. HOD- Quality Assurance is the authority for product release.

steps.heading: Colour verification at first piece approval

body.text: In order to verify the color during first piece approval concern person shall have Munsell hue test from certifying medical practitioner.
HOD-Quality Assurance shall accept the product only with proper justification where negligible deviation of product test report found with specified standard.

Reference samples, approved by customer or consumer and forwarded by Marketing, shall be properly identified by Customer Name and Quality. The reference samples shall be stored in suitable conditions to maintain their original status. Records of reference samples shall be maintained.

In order to verify the right production is going on products shall be inspected/ tested as per the specification sheet. HOD-QA is responsible for incorporated the changes in specification. Conformation of changes should be informed to Quality control department by means of hard copy or in soft media.

To aid investigation in the event of customer complaints, production samples shall be retained. Retained samples shall be properly identified by Job No., Design Name, and Date of Production. Retained samples shall bear the approval of HOD-Production and HOD-QA. The retained production samples shall be held and stored in suitable conditions to maintain their original status. Records of retained production samples shall be maintained. The retention time of the retained production samples is suitably determined by HOD-QA keeping in view the customers' or consumers' or legal requirements as well as product shelf life and the same shall also be noted in the record of retained production samples.

steps.heading: Calibration of measuring and monitoring devices

body.text: All measuring and monitoring devices, used to take/ make measurements for product safety, legality and quality, shall be calibrated as per calibration frequency defined in DS/02-04. Record of calibration shall be maintained. Further, the measuring and monitoring devices shall be suitably marked with the calibration status (calibrated on, calibration due on). Calibration status shall be cross checked by compliance officer or Quality control officer for correct information. Record for Checking of calibration sticker shall also be maintained. When the identified measuring and monitoring devices are found not to be operating within specified limits, the organization shall deploy corresponding reaction plans in order to establish the safety status of the product prior to release. This reaction plan is documented in the form of Work Instructions and shall be suitably displayed within the shop floor.

Complaints from customers shall be received through letters/ e-mails and recorded by Marketing. All complaints related to product safety, legality and quality shall be forwarded by Marketing to Quality Assurance. HOD-Quality Assurance along with HOD-Production shall investigate the customer complaints for determining the root cause and shall initiate appropriate corrective action (if any) appropriate to the seriousness and frequency of complaint issues. Result of investigation and corrective action shall be recorded in Corrective Action Report. The actions taken against complaint shall be communicated, if required, to the customer through e-mails.

Aspect Impact Analysis, Risk Hazard Analysis shall be done as per CM/DS- 1, Guide line for Environmental Aspect Impact Analysis & CM/DS- 2, Guide Line for OHS&S Hazard Identification & Risk Assessment.

blocks.text: The purpose of this procedure is to ensure that any persons performing tasks for the organization or on its behalf are competent on the basis of appropriate education, training or experience. This manual defines the methods needed to –

determine necessary competence for personnel performing work that is associated with significant Aspect Impact and Risk Hazard or affecting conformity to product requirement
provide training or take other actions to satisfy the required competence
provide a standard based on international human rights norms and national labor laws that will protect and empower all personnel, suppliers/subcontractors, sub suppliers, and home workers
adoption of a documented and effective hazard and risk management system of products
The following operations shall be within the scope of this procedure –
Competency Assessment
Preparation of training plan
Conducting training
Evaluation of effectiveness of training
Conducting awareness program
Conducting On-the-Job Training
Complying with the requirements of Social Accountability of this standard will enable a company to: -
Develop, maintain, and enforce policies and procedures in order to manage those issues which it can control or influence
Credibly demonstrate to interested parties that existing company policies and procedures and practices conform to the requirements of this standard
All employees including contractors performing tasks for the organization or on its behalf are also the scope of this procedure.

responsibilities: The prime responsibility for implementation and maintenance of this procedure shall be with the HOD-P&A. He shall be assisted by all HODs.

Any type of injury shall be reported to P&A. Concerned person in P&A shall examine the patient and render first-aid treatment. The same shall be noted in First-Aid Register.

CHILD LABOR

The company has not employed and support use of child labor anywhere. Company shall be recorded as evidence that company is not engaging any child labor within the organization. Company shall be maintained Personal Dossier (R/04-07) for the labor and Employee Personnel File (R/04-08) for the staff of the company which contain the Application form, Appointment Letters, Age Proofs (School Certificates/Dr. Certificates) Contracts with Appointment. Company shall be maintained Register of Adult Workers Contract labor (R/04- 09)

FORCED / COMPULSORY LABOR

The company has not engaged in and supports the use of forced labor anywhere.

Reference: Personal Dossier (R/04-07), Personnel File (R/04-08). Company shall maintain Register of Adult Workers Contract Labor (R/04-09)

HEALTH AND SAFETY

The company shall provide safe and healthy working environment and shall take adequate steps to prevent accidents and injury by minimizing causes of hazards inherent in the environment. Company shall be maintained Periodical Medical Examination Record (R/13-02)

FREEDOM OF ASSOCIATION AND RIGHT TO COLLECTIVE BARGAINING

The company has put in respect the right to freedom of association and collective bargaining There are no unions within the organization. But Company has appointed Workers Representative. Top Management shall conduct meeting (Minutes of Meeting between Management & Unions) (R/04-10) with worker Representative and fulfill workers’ demand.

DISCRIMINATION

The company has not followed any discriminatory policy in hiring, firing, remuneration, access to training, promotion, termination or retirement based on race, national or social origin, cast, birth, religion, disability, gender or any other condition that could give rise to discrimination(R/04-12).

DISCIPLINARY PRACTICES

The company shall be treated all personnel with dignity and respect. The company shall not engage in or tolerate the use of corporal punishment, mental or physical coercion or verbal abuse of personnel. No harsh or inhuman treatment has not been made to any employee. The company shall be established non-arbitrary and effective systems for giving written / formal warnings for such personnel or labor found under “Misconduct”. Company shall conduct meeting (Works, Grievances and Prevention of Harassment & Abuse Committee Meeting) (R/04-11). Company shall be maintained Records of Grievances and their Corrective Actions (R/04-12).

WORKING HOURS

The company has complied with applicable laws and industry standards on working hours and public holidays. The normal week as defined by law does not exceed 48 hours. Personnel provided 1 day off in every seven days. There is no requirement of Over Time with in the Organization(R/04-13).

Remuneration

The company has ensured that wages paid per standard work week meets legal and industry minimum standard (Computerized Wage Register) (R/04-13), Wage Slips (R/04-14) and sufficient to meet basic needs of personnel, providing some discretionary income. As per State Jute Associations’ Circular Minimum Wage Calculation shall be done.

Worker Representative

The company shall ensure that a representative from non-management personnel has been chosen to facilitate communication with Senior Management with matters related to labors or workers (Minutes of Meeting between Management & Unions) (R/04-10).

Control of Subcontractors

Appropriate Records of Sub- Contractors shall be maintained(R/04-15).

Communication

Outside communication and stakeholders’ engagement shall be done (DS/CM-05)

On receipt of enquiry from customer, the same shall be reviewed. Record of such review and action arising from such review shall be maintained in Order Register (R/05-01). Subsequently, based on the customer's supplied design production department shall be informed to produce a sample. On receipt of samples, the same shall be sent to customer along with the offer.

On receipt of order along with approved prototype samples, the order shall be reviewed before commitment to supply. Record of such review and action arising from such review shall be maintained in Order Register (R/05-01). Review of customer requirement shall include –

Requirement specified by customer, including delivery and post-delivery activities
Requirement not stated by customer, but necessary for specified/ intended use
Requirements related to product safety, legality and quality
Legislative requirements
Requirement of appropriate specifications or codes of practice exists for finished products.
Where customer provides no documented statement of requirement, the customer requirements are confirmed before acceptance.

Based on the customer order, Marketing shall prepare Job Order file specifying spec-sheet of design, prototype of design, bill of material, cutting-printing-stitching order, packing and labeling instruction etc. This Job Order file shall be forwarded to factory as well as to Purchase department.
When product requirements are changed, relevant documents (Job Order file) shall be amended. Subsequently concerned persons shall be intimated about the amendment.
Effective communication with customer has been implemented for communicating to customer in relation to product information, order/ enquiry handling, customer compliant, customer feedback.

All complaints would be acknowledged to the Customers within a period of 24 hours. An investigation would be initiated by the Director and root cause of the complaint would be obtained. Timeline to completion such investigation is maximum 72 hours from the time of complain received with maximum of two-week times. Confirmation of complain status as open or closed to be get from customer over email or call for future reference.

Complaints from customers shall be received through letters/ e-mails and recorded by Marketing in Customer Complaint Register (R/06-03). The actions taken against complaint (correction) shall be recorded in customer complaint register itself and shall be communicated, if required, to the customer through e-mails.

All complaints related to product safety, legality and quality shall be forwarded by Marketing to Quality Assurance. HOD-Quality Assurance along with HOD-Production shall investigate the customer complaints for determining the root cause and shall initiate appropriate corrective action (if any) appropriate to the seriousness and frequency of complaint issues. Result of investigation and corrective action shall be recorded in Corrective Action Report. The actions taken against complaint shall be communicated, if required, to the customer through e-mails.

In order to determine customer satisfaction, Customer Satisfaction Survey shall be carried out at least once in a year by distributing and collecting customer feedback form. The customer feedback shall be reviewed and customer satisfaction index shall be calculated based on the guidelines given in DS/05-02. Overall Customer Satisfaction Index shall be summarized in CSI Summary Report (R/05-04).
All necessary requirements fitting to this Process shall be maintained as per SA 8000 2008.

The purpose of this procedure is to establish a system for Purchase operation in order to ensure that purchase processes are planned and carried out under controlled condition. This procedure also defines the method needed to –

1. deal with nonconforming product
2. mitigate the Aspect –Impact and Risk- Hazard associated with the operations
3. provide a standard based on international human rights norms and national labour laws that will protect and empower all personnel, suppliers/subcontractors, sub suppliers, and home workers
4. adoption of a documented and effective hazard and risk management system of product

The following operations shall be within the scope of this procedure—

1. Procurement of Raw Materials
2. Selection and Evaluation of Suppliers for purchased products other than store items and local purchase.
3. Evaluation of performance of Purchased functions

responsibilities: The prime responsibility for implementation and maintenance of this procedure shall be with the HOD-Purchase. He shall be assisted by Sectional In charge for their respective areas of operations.

steps.heading: Purchasing Process (Raw Material / Accessories / Packing Material)

body.text: Purchase department shall contact with the suppliers for product availability, pricing and other relevant information. Enquiries shall be sent to the approved suppliers. On receipt of quotation negotiation and subsequently Purchase department shall place Purchase Order (R/06-03) to the selected supplier.

Purchase Order thus placed shall be complete in respect of product specification, quantity, delivery schedule, applicable regulatory requirements, other terms and conditions as decided by the management. Other terms and conditions may include –

Requirements for approval of product, procedures, processes and equipment’s
Inspection Criteria
Requirements of Consumer Product Management System
Purchase department shall follow-up with the supplier for timely delivery of the products.

Depending on the stock position and requirement of user, HOD-Stores shall place the Material Indent to the purchase department.

Purchase department shall purchase on two basic principles –

Purchase of materials under quarterly, six monthly or yearly contract as per price list or as per pre-negotiated terms and condition
Purchase of materials by floating inquiries

The basis of adopting different method lies on the type of materials, frequency of requirement, volume of consumption and market trend.

Enquiries shall be sent to the approved suppliers. Offers received from suppliers, against floated enquiries, shall be tabulated format with that last business discussion. Suppliers shall be selected on the basis of best terms offered. Purchase Order shall be placed with selected supplier.

Purchase Order thus placed shall be complete in respect of product specification, quantity, delivery schedule, applicable regulatory requirements, other terms and conditions as decided by the Management. Other terms and conditions may include –

Requirements for approval of product, procedures, processes and equipment’s
Inspection Criteria
Requirements of Consumer Product Management System

The competent authority shall review and approve all purchasing documents, for adequacy of specified requirements prior to release. Proper record of all communication including order copy and indent copy shall be kept properly for purpose of retrieval when needed.

Purchase department shall follow-up with the supplier for timely delivery of the products.

In case of discrepancy in specification or delivery schedule of product, the inventor shall communicate with purchase department for issue of amendment to purchase order.

Selection of new suppliers shall be based on analysis of supplier’s credential as well as actual performance during trial order. This should also be in line with the hazard and risk assessment of processes. New suppliers shall apply for registration with the organization through Supplier Registration Form (R/06-04). Placement of trial order and subsequent decision shall be taken by HOD-Purchase. On the basis of successful performance in trial order, the supplier shall be enlisted in the List of Approved Suppliers (R/06-01).

The Organization undertakes an informed decision that in case of emergency or any other situation the use of product must be approved by General Manager or Respective Merchandiser with inform to Top Management if the product specific Audit or Monitoring has not undertaken.

steps.heading: Supplier Monitoring/ Control and Supplier Evaluation

body.text:
Supplier performance shall be monitored on a regular basis (as and when materials are received and inspected at the factory). The supplier’s performance shall be summarized in Supplier Performance Report (R/06-05). The guidelines for evaluation of supplier’s performance are given in DS/06-02.

Supplier’s contractual Agreements and/ or the written commitment and commitment to social accountability shall be maintained in Records.

Evaluation of Supplier Performance Report (R/06-05) shall be done based on Lab Dip Delivery & Approval Performance, Intake Inspections Performance, Testing Performance, Delivery performance, Risk Assessment, Agree to continuous improvements of the factory.

Contentious supplier monitoring shall be performed by either visit to the supplier site or by telephonic or via soft media.

Supplier monitoring shall be done at least once in a six-month basis. Monitoring information shall be gotten from previous six months records & Verbal guidance from Purchase and Quality department on the basis of point no. 5.6.3 (Evaluation of Supplier Performance)

Based on the supplier performance over a period of time, Purchase department shall evaluate the supplier’s ability to supply products in accordance with the organization’s requirements. In case of poor performers, as evident from supplier performance report, supplier having D rating, HOD-Purchase shall decide one of the following –

De-register the supplier
Issue warning letters to the suppliers

A de-registered supplier shall be eligible for registration in the approved supplier list subject to reentry through new supplier selection process (as described in 5.5). However, maximum of two consecutive chances for re-registration shall only be allowed, falling which the suppliers shall be blacklisted.

Blacklisting of a de-registered supplier may also be affected for specific reasons (other than the above condition) at the discretion of HOD-Purchase. De-registration or Blacklisting decision shall be intimated to the corresponding supplier through formal letter.

D category supplier shall not do any business until and unless new approval taken from purchase department as maintaining the process of new supplier registration.

The company shall monitor & maintain the Product Quality, Legality & Safety in case of use of product where Audit or monitoring has not been undertaken. In such case a valid Product Test Certificate must be produced by supplier.

Aspect Impact Analysis, Risk Hazard Analysis shall be done as per CM/DS- 1, Guide line for Environmental Aspect Impact Analysis & CM/DS- 2, Guide Line for OHS&S Hazard Identification & Risk Assessment.

body.text: In order to prevent the risk of contamination and damage, the Storage and Preservation Criteria of finished products shall be established by HOD- Production & Maintenance and the same shall be recorded in R/07-05. In case of materials having specific storage and preservation criteria, the same shall be stored under that specific condition.

body.text: Based on dispatch schedule, as intimated through Job Order by Marketing, packing supervisor shall plan for packing of finished products. Accordingly material requisition (packing material, labels, accessories etc.) shall be raised to stores. Manpower requirement shall also be planned by concerned packing supervisor.

steps.heading: Packaging standard and packing and labeling

body.text: In order to protect the finished product from contamination and damage during transit and storage, appropriate packaging standard in line with the customers’/ countries’ requirement shall be developed and the same shall be recorded in Job order file. Product packaging shall be appropriate for the intended use and stored under conditions to minimize the risk of contamination and deterioration. Packing and labeling shall be done as per customer’s requirement, as mentioned in Job Order file.
If required by customer, legible batch coding shall be mentioned on the primary packaging and the outer pack.

Packed finished products shall be stored at pre-defined storage area within the shop floor. Accordingly, stock shall be updated (R/07-02). In order to ensure that packed finished products of different specification are not inadvertently mixed, products are properly identified and stored within the finished goods stores.

steps.heading: Cross verification of daily packing production

body.text: Cross verification of daily Packing production shall be tallied with pass Metal detection bag register. Finishing In-charge shall responsible for this daily checking.

steps.heading: Storage and preservation criteria of packed products

body.text: In order to prevent the risk of contamination and damage, the Storage and Preservation Criteria of packed products shall be established by HOD-Packing & Dispatch and the same shall be recorded in R/07-05.

steps.heading: Physical and chemical control of packed products

body.text: Where physical and chemical control of packed products is required to ensure product safety, legality and quality, the Storage and Preservation Criteria shall be established (R/07-05). The same shall also be suitably displayed at relevant locations.

All dispatchable products shall be inspected as quality assurance plan by QA department. No product shall be dispatched unless pre-dispatch inspection is satisfactorily completed. HOD- Quality Assurance is the authority for product release. Inspection results shall be maintained in concerned inspection reports.

Dispatch Advice shall be received from Shipment section (HO) in the form of Lorry Pass. On receipt of lorry pass, concerned dispatch supervisor shall check the availability of concerned product in the stock and accordingly shall prepare necessary dispatch related documents (GP- 1, ARE-1, Gate Pass).

On receipt of vehicle, the same shall be checked/ inspected by QA personnel. On receipt of clearance by concerned QA personnel, packed products shall be loaded into the vehicle (container) under the supervision of dispatch supervisor. Where the product transported is susceptible to weather damage, vehicle shall be properly covered.
Reconciliation of Physical Stock Vs ERP Stock shall be performed on weekly basis by HOD- Packing & Dispatch.

steps.heading: Damaged products found during physical verification

body.text: In case of products found damaged during physical verification, the same shall be treated as per method described in the Guide Lines for Control of Nonconforming Product (DS/CM- 13).

The purpose of this procedure is to establish hazard and risk management process in order to ensure that all hazards to consumer safety and legality are identified and appropriate controls documented, implemented and maintained.
The entire product realization process, from receipt of raw materials, accessories, product- contact materials to dispatch of end products to customers/ consumers shall be within the scope of this procedure.
To identify the activity and simultaneously impact on environment and health with control measures
No product is intended for children use. If any product is made only for children's purposes, in that case Risk Assessment for that particular product should be done separately so that hazard should be identified and mitigate for consumer safety and legality point of view.
The prime responsibility for implementation and maintenance of this procedure shall be with the System Manager He shall be assisted by a multi-disciplinary team comprises of all HODs.
None

body.text:
All relevant information (inputs) needed to conduct the hazard analysis shall be collected, maintained, updated and documented. The inputs for hazard analysis are –
Product Information – Raw Materials, Accessories, Product Safety, Product-contact Materials
Product Information – End Products (including intended use of end products)
Process Information – Process Flow Diagram
Process Information – Process Steps and Control Measures
Legislative Requirements – Safety and legal requirements of the country were sold and country where manufactured

The team shall define and document up-to-date Product Information for all raw materials, accessories and product-contact materials (R/09-01) as well as for all end products (R/11-02) to the extent needed to conduct the hazard analysis. This information shall be approved by HOD-Production.
Verification of product information shall be done at least once in six months and accordingly the same shall be modified/ updated. Records of verification and subsequent modifications/ updating shall be maintained (R/09-10).

The team shall prepare up-to-date Process Flow Diagram (R/09-03) for the products. This includes process steps as well as sequence and interaction of process steps. The team shall also define and document up-to-date Process Information (R/09-04) in accordance with the process flow diagram. This includes existing control measures, process parameters and applicable procedures.
Verification of process information shall be done at least once in six months through on-site checking and accordingly the same shall be modified/ updated. Records of verification and subsequent modifications/ updating shall be maintained (R/09-10).

All legislative requirements relating to the product safety and legality of the product for the country in which they are to be sold, including requirements concerning the labeling of the product shall be identified. The same shall be recorded in Legal Register (R/CM-04).
HOD-Marketing shall be in touch with the customers/ consumers and other statutory & regulatory bodies for obtaining information about any amendments in legislative requirements or new legislative requirements. In case of any change and/ or inclusion in legislative requirements, the legal register shall be amended to keep it up-to-date.
Verification of legislative requirements shall be done once in a year through evaluation of compliance with legislative requirements and accordingly the legal register shall be modified/ updated. Records of verification and subsequent modifications/ updating shall be maintained (R/09-10).

steps.heading: Product Safety, Quality and Legality Requirements

body.text:
Product Safety and quality related risk is addressed in Risk assessment study.
Based on risk assessment study Critical Control Point and Operation Control Point is identified and addressed in document no R/09/08 and R/09-09
Hazard Analysis
The team shall identify all hazards (along with the steps at which hazards introduced) that are reasonably expected to occur in relation to the type of product, type of process and actual processing facilities. For each of the hazards identified, the acceptance level of the hazards in the end product shall be determined taking into account established statutory and regulatory requirements, customer's/ consumer's requirements (if any), the intended use by the customer/ consumer and other relevant data. The same shall be recorded in Hazard Analysis Worksheet (R/09-06).
The team shall assess the level of risk for the identified hazards as per the guidelines given in DS/09-01. The result of hazard assessment shall also be recorded in Hazard Analysis Worksheet (R/09-06).
Verification of hazard analysis shall be done at least once in six months and accordingly the same shall be modified/ updated. Records of verification and subsequent modifications/ updating shall be maintained (R/09-10).
Hazard assessment shall be updated annually. In case of any changes Critical Control Point and Operation Control Point is according revised and record shall be maintained in document no R/09/08 and R/09-09
The organization does not intentionally use Persistent Organic Pollutants (POPs) or generate associated POP-containing waste. In case of any change, chemical assessment shall be reviewed and updated accordingly and records shall be maintained.

Guideline for Environmental Aspect – Impact is detailed discussed in (DS/CM-01) both for Normal / Abnormal condition and Emergency Condition. Process based detail study shall be done (R/CM-01) and shall be reviewed at least once in a year.
Occupation Health & Safety guideline is detail discussed in (DS/09-01). Study in Occupational Health & Safety hazard is done in (R/CM-03). Review of this study shall be done at least once in a year.
Depending on the level of risk, an appropriate risk-based control measure shall be selected, as per the following guidelines, which is capable of preventing, eliminating or reducing the hazards to defined acceptance level.

rows: For this type of hazard, its elimination or reduction to acceptance level is essential. If it is not possible to reduce the risk, work has to remain prohibited.
Risk Control Measures are Action Plan for Elimination, Operational Controls and HACCP Plan, which ensures that the risk is reduced.

Decision Tree (DS/09-02) shall be used for determining the appropriate risk control measures. If CCP is identified, then proper HACCP Plan shall be established (R/09-09); otherwise, Operational Control shall be established (R/09-08)
For this type of hazard, efforts should be made to reduce the risk level. Risk Control Measures are sometimes Operational Control (R/09-08) or Action Plan for Elimination
For this type of hazard, no additional controls are required. Work can be continued under normal operating condition.

body.text:
Prior to implementation of control measures, as defined in Operational Control and/ or HACCP Plan, the team shall validate that –
the selected control measures are capable of achieving the intended control of the hazards for which they are designated
the control measures are effective and capable of (in combination) ensuring control of the identified hazards to obtain end products that meet the defined acceptance levels
If the result of the validation (R/09-11) shows nonconformity, the control measures shall be modified and re-assessed.
Verification of Operational Control as well as HACCP Plan shall be done at least once in six months and accordingly Operational Control or HACCP Plan shall be modified/ updated. Records of verification and subsequent modifications/ updating shall be maintained (R/09- 10).

In order to demonstrate that the control measures are in place all the time, all control measures (HACCP Plan, Operational Control) shall be monitored against measurable limits as per defined frequency. The monitoring results shall be recorded in different departmental registers.
When limits are exceeded, planned corrections and corrective actions, as specified in the HACCP Plan or Operational Control, shall be taken. These actions shall ensure that the cause of nonconformity is identified, the parameters are brought back under control and recurrence is prevented.

In case of changes in the design, formulation, process, raw materials or legislation, HOD- Production shall determine whether it is necessary to review the hazard analysis, the established Operational Control and the HACCP Plan.
Based on the above evaluation and subsequent review, the elements of hazard and risk management shall be updated.

body.text: In order to facilitate effective product recall and withdrawal, the following facilities are made available within the organization –

body.text: The organization has established a forward traceability system in order to track the dispatches to customer(s). Each and every dispatch must accompany with relevant dispatch related documents (GP-1, ARE-1), one copy of which is kept in dispatch section for further reference purposes. In case of unsafe products being dispatched to customer(s), the products can be tracked from those dispatch related documents.

In case of product recall, prior intimation to relevant parties (transporter, customer) shall be given at appropriate time by HOD-Packing & Dispatch with the help of HOD-Marketing. A list of contact numbers (R/11-01) shall be developed and maintained for this purpose.

steps.heading: Arrange transport to bring back product

body.text: Suitable transports shall be arranged by HOD-Packing & Dispatch in order to bring back the product. A list of transporters (R/11-02) shall be developed and maintained for this purpose.

steps.heading: Receipt, storage and disposition of recovered products

body.text: On receipt of unsafe products, the products shall be stored at pre-defined location within the organization. The stock shall be updated to incorporate the stock return. Decision shall be taken jointly by HOD-Quality Assurance and HOD-Production about the disposition of recovered products. Accordingly, the recovered products shall be disposed of by cutting into small pieces so that in line of disposal it shall prevent use in anywhere. Record of such disposition action shall be maintained.

The organization shall conduct mock drill of this product recall procedure (both forward and backward traceability) at least once in every year. And for internal traceability at least twice in a year. Performances during the mock drills shall be observed by designated Observers. The Observations/ shortcomings shall be reviewed by HOD-Packing & Dispatch and recommendations shall be made for further improvement. A detailed report on the mock drill (R/16-03) along with deficiencies observed and corrective action taken shall be made available.

In event of Product recall all concern person shall be coordinate. Emergency contact person should always be available and a systematic procedure by bring together for return back the materials from supply chain / end customer shall me closely monitored.
We shall have written agreement in place with distributor and other parties in the supply chain where this are necessary to ensure effective Recall or Withdrawal.

In the event of the product recall the certification body issuing the BRC Certificate and the appropriate enforcement authority (egg: Customs, Excise, Sales Tax, etc.) shall be informed within 15 days from such recall incidents. Organization shall also communicate exhaustively with our buyers to understand and adhere to any Legal reporting obligations in the regions of sales.

The purpose of this procedure is to have a system in order to keep the site environment clean and tidy and to reduce the possibility of contamination from natural sources, day-to-day plant operations.
Entire plant, covering all site locations, are within the scope of this procedure.

The prime responsibility for implementation and maintenance of this procedure shall be with the Management Representative and Cleaning Responsible Supervisor. Supervisor shall be assisted by all HODs for their respective areas of operation.
None

body.text:
In charge-Housekeeping in consultation with concerned HOD shall develop housekeeping schedule covering all site locations and the same shall be recorded in Housekeeping Schedule (R/12-01).
Appropriate housekeeping shall be carried out as per housekeeping schedule in order to maintain all site locations in good and cleaned condition. Necessary work instructions shall be developed, if required, by in charge-Housekeeping in order to facilitate effective housekeeping operation. Records of housekeeping shall be maintained in Housekeeping Record (R/12-02).
Adequate lighting has been provided for all work areas in order to facilitate effective housekeeping. This is the responsibility of in charge-Housekeeping.
In order to reduce any risk to product safety, legality and quality from glass windows, ceramics, bulbs and strip lights, electric fly-killer units etc., special work instruction shall be developed to facilitate effective housekeeping operation.
All glass in factory shall be counted and fortnightly checking shall be done to monitor in case of any breakage or missing. All such incident shall be recorded and inform the General Manager and Quality Manager for necessary corrective and preventive action.
Effectiveness of housekeeping activities shall be judged by conducting housekeeping audit at least once in a month. The audit shall be conducted by auditors independent of the area being audited. The audit result shall be recorded in Housekeeping Audit Report (R/12-03). The audit result shall be reviewed by Management Representative and in charge- Housekeeping and accordingly necessary actions shall be decided.

In order to restrict the entry of pests, suitable pest control devices (such as pest-o-flash, rodent killing machine) shall be installed at suitable locations within the factory premises. In order to reduce the risk to product safety, legality and quality, in charge-Housekeeping in consultation with concerned HOD shall develop a Pest Control Plan (R/12-04) considering the nature of activities, location, neighboring environment.
In order to deter and eradicate pest infestation, appropriate pest control activities (inspection, treatment etc.) are being carried out as per pest control plan. For this purpose, services of competent pest control organization have been rendered. The nature of pest control activities and area coverage shall be clearly defined in their Service Contract. Records of pest control activities shall be maintained in Pest Control Record (R/12-05).
If desired by customer or otherwise required, raw materials shall be fumigated in order to neutralize the effect of pest infestation. Corresponding records of fumigation shall be kept in Pest Control Record (R/12-05).
Use and application of baits, insecticide sprays and fungicides shall be done after prior risk assessment followed by imposition of operational control. This information shall be properly communicated to concerned pest control organization.
Effectiveness of pest control activities shall be judged by conducting housekeeping audit at least once in a month. The audit shall be conducted by auditors independent of the area being audited. The audit result shall be recorded in Housekeeping Audit Report (R/12-03). The audit result shall be reviewed by Management Representative and accordingly necessary actions (e.g. continuation of Service Contract) shall be decided.

steps.heading: Waste Management

body.text:
In order to facilitate proper collection, collation and disposal of waste material generated from process, in charge-Housekeeping in consultation with HOD-Production shall develop a Waste Management Plan (R/12-06).
In order to prevent the accumulation of solid waste in production areas, regular waste collection shall be carried out as per waste management plan. The wastes shall be disposed of at specified location outside the production areas in order to minimize risk to the product.

Further, access to all areas shall be restricted to authorized personnel only. Visitors are not allowed to enter factory premises without proper authorization of designated personnel.

steps.heading: Internal Sorting & Disposal of Waste According to Waste Streams

body.text:
Waste Stream Categorization: Waste is sorted based on specific waste streams to enhance disposal and recycling. Sorting bins and designated collection points are clearly marked for each waste type:
Wood Waste: Recovered from packaging and processing, sorted for potential reuse.
Electronic Waste (E-Waste): Items like electronic parts, cables, and batteries, collected in dedicated bins and sent to certified e-waste recyclers.
Electrical Wires and Scrap Metals: Collected separately for recycling or resale.
Glass and Plastics: Collected separately for recycling
Disposal Methods:
Reuse and Recycling: Sorted materials are reviewed for reuse, repurposing, or recycling through approved vendors.
Waste Log Maintenance: The Waste Sorting Log (GJ-R/WM-01) records the type, volume, and disposal method for each waste stream.

responsibilities: The prime responsibility for implementation and maintenance of this procedure shall be with the Medical Officer. The organization may consult with external occupational health specialists as well as medical practitioners in this regard.

rows.definition: Identifiable, adverse physical or mental condition arising from and/ or made worse by a work activity and/ or work-related situation.

Conditions and factors that affect, or could affect, the health and safety of employees or other workers (including temporary workers and contractor personnel), visitors, or any other person in the workplace.

body.text:
A detailed health hazard survey shall be carried out throughout the organization in order to determine –
Different hazardous working conditions to which the employees are exposed to while working
Occupational health hazards that are associated with those hazardous working conditions
Number of employees (including name of individuals) who are exposed to those hazardous working conditions
Type of medical tests to be carried out against those occupational health hazards and its frequency
Frequency of medical tests shall be determined on the basis of –
The natural history of the disease, including the rapidity with which the biochemical, morphological, behavioral etc. changes might occur or be detected by screening test
The level of exposure to the hazardous agent and to any other interacting agent(s)
The anticipated susceptibility of the exposed population and individuals
The organization may consult with external occupational health specialists as well as medical practitioners in this regard.
The survey results shall be reported in Health Hazard Survey Report (R/13-01).
The health hazard survey shall be repeated at least once in three (3) years to find out improvements in organizational performances as well as new hazardous working conditions for new or modified activities, products or services.

As indicated in the health hazard survey report, the concerned employees shall undergo specific medical checkup as per defined frequency. The organization may consult with external medical practitioners in this regard. The medical checkup reports shall be kept along with the health card of the individual employees.
Apart from this, each and every employee shall undergo a yearly routine health checkup. The Medical Officer shall examine the person and shall report his findings in Medical Examination Report (Pre-Employment/ Periodical) (R/13-02).
Every employee can report confidentially to Medical Officer for any suspected occupational health problem. On the other hand, Medical Officer shall report employee confidentially when routine health checkup or specific medical checkup uncover a potential health problem.
Medical Officer is the custodian of all medical reports. An employee is eligible to access only his medical reports.
Authorized medical team shall review the medical reports (including the trends) of employees as and when required and shall take suitable actions in order to mitigate the health problem of employees as well as safeguard the health of the employees.

Any new employee (Permanent or Temporary, Apprentice or Trainee) shall undergo a pre-employment medical checkup on receipt of intimation from Departmental Head (P&A). The Medical Officer shall examine the person and shall report his findings in Medical Examination Report (Pre-Employment/ Periodical) (R/13-02).

Medical services are provided to the employees round the clock although Doctors are available for consultation on selective time basis which varies from time to time.
Any type of injury and/ or occupational illness shall be reported to health center by the concerned sectional in charge through First Aid Intimation Slip. Nurse along with the Attendant (if necessary) shall examine the patient and render first-aid treatment as appropriate. The same shall be recorded in OPD Register (R/13-03).
Every department shall have a spillage kit to managing any bodily fluid spillage like vomiting and bleeding within the production and storage area. In case of such emergency person shall be use this kit to prevent the product or person contamination. Immediate cleaning of such fluid shall be performed by departmental housekeeping staff.
In case further investigation is felt required, the same shall be consulted with the Medical Officer on his availability. The nature of disease and treatment/ advice given to the employee shall be noted in the Work Injury Review (R/13-04).
Ambulance Van with necessary apparatus is available round the clock to render service to the patient.

The pharmacist shall supply the medicine to the patient depending upon availability of medicine in stock(R/13-05).; otherwise, the prescription shall be given to the patient for own purchase. The pharmacist shall maintain the stock of medicine in the Medicine Stock Register.
Medicines are procured through purchase department as and when required based on the indent raised by pharmacist. On receipt of medicine, corresponding stock of medicine shall be updated in the Medicine Stock Register.
Physical verifications of stock of medicine shall be conducted on monthly basis to update the stock register and to segregate the medicines which have lapsed the expiry date. These expired medicines shall be disposed of in safe manner (discussed later).

rows: Waste Sharps / (needles, syringes, blades, scalpels, glass etc. that may cause puncture and cuts; this includes both used and unused sharps)
Discarded Medicines / (waste comprising of outdated, contaminated and discarded medicines)

body.text:
Bio-medical waste shall not be mixed with other wastes. Bio-medical waste shall be segregated into containers/ bags at the point of generation. No untreated bio-medical waste shall be kept stored beyond a period of 48 hours.
Chemical treatment shall be performed using at least 1% hypochlorite solution or any other equivalent chemical reagent. It must be ensured that chemical treatment ensures disinfection. Destruction/ Shredding must be such so as to prevent unauthorized reuse.
For disposition of waste in secured landfill, a pit shall be dug about 2 meters deep. It shall be half filled with waste, then covered with lime within 50 cm of the surface, before filling the rest of the pit with soil. On each occasion, when wastes are added to the pit, a layer of 10 cm of soil shall be added to cover wastes.
It shall be ensured that animals do not have any access to the pit. Covers of galvanized iron/ wire meshes may be used. The site should be relatively impermeable and no shallow well should be close to the site. The pit should be distant from habitation so as to ensure that no contamination occurs of any surface water or ground water. The area should not be prone to flooding or erosion.
The disposition shall be done under close and dedicated supervision. The record of waste generation and disposition in pit shall be maintained as per R/13-06.
The organization shall submit an Annual Report in Form II by 31st January every year, to declare information about the categories and quantities of bio-medical wastes handled during the preceding year.

Medical Officer in association with Training department, shall organize First-aid Training for employees. Awareness trainings shall also be conducted on health-related issues from time to time.
The instruments used for medical checkup is at the sole responsibility of medical officers regarding its fitness. Medical instruments shall be calibrated as per defined frequency. A list of such equipment along with the schedule shall be maintained.
Records of such calibration (both internal and external) as well as maintenance activities of equipment shall be maintained. In case of external calibration, original calibration certificate of the equipment under calibration shall also be retained.

The purpose of this procedure is to ensure safety of the employees working in the plant as well as the machines/ equipment.
The purpose is also to have a system for firefighting related activities.
All activities related to firefighting as well as safety of employees, machines/ equipment shall be within the scope of this procedure.

In time of Fire Mock Drill Team Leader will be responsible for informing Rescue Team Members about their responsibilities along with Supervisors and Managers.
Team Members are responsible for activate Fire Alarm.

Silent Observer is responsible for noting the all record which includes Worker's evacuation through marked evacuation route, assembled in the assembly zone and attendance along with any inconsistence identified in time of Mock Drill.
Security Guards are responsible for checking all nooks and corners inside the building including outside Toilets to ensure nobody stayed behind.

They are also responsible for made off power supply and checking of emergency lights to confirm all are in working condition.

body.text: In case of Fire incident, the person noticing fire shall immediately give Fire Call (as per pre- defined phone number) to the HSCO, trained in firefighting will immediately rush to the location for dealing with fire. The organization may seek help from outside emergency services (fire brigade, medical services etc.) as well as neighboring industries in regard to fire fighting and mitigation of its consequences.

For major fire, which may lead to on-site disasters, the information shall be communicated to all the persons inside the factory through centrally operated siren. For this purpose, type of sirens and its inherent meaning shall be pre-defined and shall be communicated to all employees through awareness programmed, notice boards etc. The information shall also be communicated to the Top Management telephonically by the concerned security officer.

HSCO is responsible for maintaining all kinds of firefighting equipment. A list of Fire Fighting Equipment (including Portable Fire Extinguisher) along with their actual location shall be maintained (R/14-01). Apart from this, the department shall also maintain a layout showing Fire Hydrant System.
Routine check-up and repairing of the firefighting equipment as well as procurement of spares shall be the responsibility of the HSCO.

As a matter of statutory requirement, safety committee meeting shall be conducted once in a month to discuss the safety related issues. Safety committee has equal representation of workmen and management staffs.
The input to Safety Committee Meeting shall include –

Incident statistics for the last month
Status of incident investigation and recommended action
Survey results of unsafe acts/ practices and unsafe procedures/ conditions
Follow-up action from previous safety committee meeting
Resource needs, status of training and its effectiveness
Recommendations for improvement
In addition to the above, the following issues shall also be taken up as an agenda of the safety committee meeting, as and when required –

hazard identification, risk assessments and determination of controls
incident investigation and analysis
development and review of Environment & OHS&s policy, Environmental and OH&S objectives and targets
The output from the Safety Committee Meeting shall include any decision and actions related to –

Incident (accident and near-miss) investigation and analysis
Resources including training requirements
Environmental and OH&S policy, environmental and OH&S objectives and targets
Hazard identification, risk assessments and determination of controls

Any decision/ action as decided in the meeting shall be documented in Safety Committee Meeting Register (R/14-02) and shall be implemented with undue delay by the concerned responsible person. Necessary follow-up with the concerned department regarding implementation of remedial measures/ recommendation shall be done by the HSCO.
Any pending points, against which no action could be decided in the safety committee meeting, shall be forwarded to the Management Review Meeting for appropriate action.
HSCO in association with Training department, shall organize “Training on Fire Fighting” for employees. Awareness trainings shall also be conducted on security related issues from time to time.
Similarly, HSCO in association with Training department, shall organize Safety Training for employees. Awareness trainings shall also be conducted on safety related issues from time to time.
Platform training for contract labors shall be conducted from time to time wherein environment, health, safety related awareness shall be given to all the contract labors present on that date.
Each and every new entrant shall be given a basic Fire Safety training which includes Fire Safety instruction, Fire Evacuation, operation of Fire extinguisher & Hose Drill etc.
Safety Induction for the new entrants (Contract Labor and Direct Labor) shall be given by the HSCO along with the concerned department.
Training for new entrants shall be done within a week from his or her joining date.

All kinds of promotional activities such as Celebration of National Safety Week, World Environment Day, Fire Service Day etc. shall be organized by the Safety/ Security Department in coordination with other departments/ functions. Record of such promotional activities shall be maintained.
As a matter of enhancing employee motivation, competitions on quiz, essay, slogans and posters, related to fire and safety may be arranged from time to time.
The details of this process are described in the procedure CM/DS-05 GUIDELINES: PARTICIPATION, CONSULTATION AND COMMUNICATION
Personal Protective Equipment are procured through purchase department as and when required based on the indent raised by Security Officer.
PPE shall be issued by the Security Department as per the requisition of different departments. Record of issue shall be maintained in PPE Issue Register (R/14-03).
However, it is the responsibility of individual department regarding usage of PPE during day- to-day operations/ activities.

PPE usage level shall be monitored by conducting independent survey of unsafe acts/ practices on a quarterly basis. The survey results shall be analyzed by Management Representative and accordingly corrective action shall be taken. Unsafe acts/ practices may result in Behavioral Safety Issues, Resource Needs.

sops.title: Procedure for Document and Record Control

blocks.text:
The purpose of this procedure is to establish a system to define controls needed to –
Approve documents for adequacy prior to issue.
Review and update as necessary and re-approve documents.
Ensure that changes and the current revision status of documents are identified.
Ensure that relevant versions of applicable documents are distributed and available at the relevant points of use.
Ensure that documents remain legible and readily identifiable.
Ensure that documents of external origin are identified and their distribution controlled
Prevent the unintended use of obsolete documents.
Apply suitable identification of obsolete documents that are retained for any purpose.
The purpose is also to establish a system to control all records related to the documented consumer product management system of the organization for ensuring the following –
Evidence of conformity to requirements and of the effective operation of the consumer product management system
Records remain legible, readily identifiable and retrievable.
Controls needed for the identification (including collation), maintenance (including review, protection), storage, retrieval, retention and disposition of records are established.
All the documents related to the consumer product management system of the organization including the documents of external origin (such as standards, code of practices) are within the scope of this procedure.

responsibilities: The prime responsibility for implementation and maintenance of this procedure shall be with the Management Representative. He shall be assisted by Document Controller for controlling of documents and by all HODs for controlling of records.

blocks.text: None

body.text: The process flow chart, showing the sequence and interactions of document control sub- processes, is given in DS/15-01.

The consumer product management system document of the organization consists of Apex Manual (Level-1 document) and procedures (Level-2 document). The procedures have the reference of Datasheets and Report Formats (Level-3 and Level-4 document).
Apex Manual is identified by the name itself. It is divided into several sections. Each section is identified by a unique section number (AM/Sec-X, where X is a unique number for a section) and section title. Annexures as referred in the manual are also a part of the document. Each annexure is identified by a unique annexure number (AM/Ann-X, where X is a unique number for a section) and annexure title.
The procedure is identified by a unique procedure number and procedure title.
The procedures consist of the following integral parts –
The main body of the procedure, referred as Procedure.
Datasheet – identified by DS/XX-ZZ, where XX is the procedure number and ZZ is running serial number (unique for one datasheet). Also identified by datasheet title.
Report Format – identified by R/XX-ZZ, where XX is the procedure number and ZZ is running serial number (unique for one report format). Also identified by report title.

steps.heading: Issue and Revision Status of Document

body.text: The issue status of a document is identified by Issue Number whereas revision status of a document is identified by Revision Number and Revision Date. Issue Number, Revision Number and Revision Date are mentioned in each and every page of document. The issue shall start from 1 and revision number shall start from 0. In case of any minor document revision, the revision number shall be incremented by 1, while issue number remains the same. Document Date will be accordingly change with each Revision or New Issue of the same. In case of document update the document, date shall be remained same. In case major document revision (such as addition/ deletion of major processes, integration of system with other management system etc.), the issue number shall be incremented by 1 and revision number shall be re-started from 0.

steps.heading: Master Copy, Controlled Copy, Obsolete Copy of Document

body.text:
The copy bearing the signature of the reviewing and approving authority shall be considered as the ‘Master Copy’. This shall be kept with Document Controller.
The copies of the master copy bearing the stamped “Controlled Copy” shall be considered as the ‘Controlled Copy’. The controlled copies shall be distributed to copy- holders as per Document Distribution list (R/15-05).
The old master copies, which are retained for archival purpose, bearing the stamp “Obsolete Copy” shall be considered as ‘Obsolete Copy’.

All the documents shall be reviewed and approved prior to use. The Apex Manual shall be reviewed and approved by Director. The documented procedures shall be reviewed and approved by the concerned persons as per List of Document Reviewing and Approving Authority (DS/15-02).
Latest version of Controlled documents shall be updated whenever any addition, deletion or introduction of new records

The controlled copies of the document shall be distributed to copy-holders as per Document Distribution list (R/15-05). Distribution of new/ amended documents shall be recorded in Document Distribution Record (R/15-01).

The person seeking the change of any document or its part shall prepare Amendment Request (R/15-02) and shall take approval from concerned reviewing and approving authority. The approved amendment request shall be forwarded to Management Representative for his review and approval.
The approved changes shall be incorporated in the document-by-Document Controller. The issue and revision status shall be updated. Subsequently Amendment Control Register (R/15- 03) shall be updated.
After incorporating necessary changes, the Document Controller shall incorporate the change in the Master Copy and issue the controlled copies to all the copy-holders. Distribution of amended documents shall be recorded in Document Distribution Record (R/15-01).
The copy-holders shall incorporate the amended pages in their controlled copy and return the old copies, if any, to Document Controller. The old controlled copies of the document shall be destroyed except the old master copy, which shall be stamped “Obsolete Copy” and kept for archival and reference purpose.

The Documents of External Origin include National/ International Standards, Statutory and Regulatory Acts and Rules, Guidance, Specification, Instruction Manuals etc. related to the documented consumer product management system of the organization.
A list of documents of external origin (R/15-04) shall be maintained by the Document Controller. Custodian of master copies of the external origin document shall be the Document Controller. The Document Controller shall issue photocopies of external origin documents based on the request from user. Records of such issues shall be maintained by the Document Controller.

Records can be stored in files or in register. The files or register shall be indexed and stored in suitable rack/cabinets. The responsibility shall lie with the respective prime responsible person. The records related to a department/ function shall be protected by the prime responsible person of the department/ function.
The records shall be kept for a minimum period, termed as Retention Period. The retention period of each record shall be decided considering legislation requirements and/ or finished product life. This is specified in the respective procedure. The disposition of records subsequent to the minimum retention time shall be done as per convenience by concerned person.
Any amendments to records shall be appropriately authorized by the concerned originator and/ or concerned custodian of the record.
In case of such amendment’s justification shall also be mentioned in a note.
Where necessary this shall be informed to concerned originator and required appropriate authorization also.

body.text: Two-way communication sessions, such as Town Halls or department meetings, will be scheduled annually. blocks.text: The purpose of this procedure is to ensure that –

The implemented consumer product management system conforms to the planned arrangements according to the requirements of Standard and to the consumer product management system requirements established by the organization.
The implemented consumer product management system is maintained and is effective in line with the organization’s Consumer Product Policy, Objectives and Targets.
The total documented consumer product management system, including Internal Audit, shall be within the scope of this procedure.

responsibilities: The prime responsibility for implementation and maintenance of this procedure shall be with the Chief of Internal Audit. He shall be assisted by competent Internal Auditors.

rows.definition: Non-fulfillment of specified requirements
There is a critical failure to comply with a safety or legal issue.

There is a substantial failure to meet any requirement of the standard and/ or a situation which, on the basis of available objective evidence, raises significant doubt as to the conformity of the product being supplied.
