body.text: Chief of Internal Audit shall prepare Internal Audit Plan (R/16-01) taking into consideration of the followings –

substeps.text: Status and importance of the operations related with consumer product management system
Importance of the operations related to product safety, legality and quality
Results of previous audits

body.text: Based on the frequency of internal audit, as mentioned in Internal Audit Plan, an Internal Audit Schedule (R/16-03) shall be prepared by the Chief of Internal Audit and the same shall be circulated to all concerned.

Internal Audits shall be carried out by competent Internal Auditors independent of those having direct responsibilities for the activity being examined. Chief of Internal Auditor shall maintain a List of Internal Auditors (R/16-02).
Before going for audit, Internal Auditor shall prepare Internal Audit Checklist cum Observation Sheet (R/16-04) by consulting the following –

substeps.text: Hazard and Risk associated with the concerned operations
The BRC Standard
Previous Checklist and Nonconformity report, if any

body.text: During audit, Internal Auditor shall write down the observations against each check point. In case of any nonconformity detected, the same shall be recorded in the Internal Audit Nonconformity Report (R/16-05).

steps.heading: Quality Assurance Plan and facilities review

body.text: Auditor shall check Quality Assurance Plan in time of Audit for necessary changes in conform to actual practice. Quality related facilities like identification of designated area for quality checking, sufficient lighting, disposal facilities etc. shall also be reviewed by auditor for all departments including quality lab. In case of any requirement or modification is required same shall be recorded in audit observation sheet.
Auditor should check Mechanical Tools, List of Machines, Tools issue & receive and integrity of tools available in production floor.

Auditor is also responsible for verification of control samples in production floor compare with tamper proof prototype preserved under lock & key and register. Discrepancies shall be recorded in audit observation sheet.

List of Measuring and Monitoring devices shall be verified during review of quality assurance procedure. Calibration Status of each device shall be reviewed from master list of calibration. In case any measuring and monitoring device which is not in use for the purpose, same shall be recorded in master list with reason.

During site tour by the internal auditor cross checking of identification marking for 100% of semi-finished or finished goods shall be cross verified to establish and check the traceability is maintained. In case of any missing same has to be reported in site tour.

Internal Audit for Quality Assurance shall include the condition of lights and intensity as per standard requirement based on buyer standard. Most stringent requirement shall be followed during implementation and cross verification of the light intensity.

Internal Audit to cross verify of complain status correctly mention with supporting details. Sufficient information shall be furnished to the customer against each complain and closer of such complain shall be recorded in complain handling register.
For confirm the correct and updated documents in use Internal Audit to check as a confirmation of updated version is in used in floor and same shall be reflected in controlled documents (DS/15-01)

Corrective action against the detected nonconformities shall be mutually decided by the auditor and the auditee and the same shall be recorded in the internal audit nonconformity report itself along with the target date for completion.
After completing the audit, Internal Auditor shall submit the Internal Audit Checklist cum Observation Sheet to the Chief of Internal Audit.

Chief of Internal Audit shall coordinate the follow-up audits for verifying the implementation and effectiveness of the corrective and/ or preventive action in respect of reported nonconformities. Timeline for completion of nonconformity is 60 days for Minor NC, 30 days for Major NC & 7 days for Critical NC. The result of follow-up audit shall be recorded in the Internal Audit Nonconformity Report itself.
After follow-up audit, Internal Auditor shall submit the Internal Audit Nonconformity Report to the Chief of Internal Audit.
Chief of Internal Audit shall prepare Internal Audit Summary Report (R/16-06) and shall forward the same for Management Review Meeting.

Apart from the departmental Internal Audit a separate Internal Audit based on BRC Standard shall be done at least once in a year which should be cover all the applicable clause of BRC General Merchandise Issue - 4.
BRC Internal Audit shall be documented in GJPL/BRC/YEAR/NO to assess the GAP analysis with the current status.

steps.heading: Deviation from Critical Limits for Critical Control Points

body.text: Data derived from the monitoring of Critical Control Points (CCPs) shall be evaluated by HOD-Production and appropriate action (correction) shall be taken immediately to bring the process or system back into control. Records of such action taken shall be recorded in the CCP Monitoring Report.

Further, HOD-Production along with HOD-Quality Assurance shall investigate the nonconformities for determining the root cause and shall initiate appropriate corrective action (if any). Result of investigation and corrective action shall be recorded in Corrective Action Report (R/17-01).

Complaints from customers shall be received through letters/ e-mails and recorded by Marketing in Customer Complaint Register. The actions taken against complaint (correction) shall be recorded in customer complaint register itself and shall be communicated, if required, to the customer through e-mails.

All complaints related to product safety, legality and quality shall be forwarded by Marketing to Quality Assurance. HOD-Quality Assurance along with HOD-Production shall investigate the customer complaints for determining the root cause and shall initiate appropriate corrective action (if any). Result of investigation and corrective action shall be recorded in Corrective Action Report (R/17-01). The actions taken against complaint shall be communicated, if required, to the customer through e-mails.
Action against non-compliance with legislative requirements shall be initiated immediately by HOD-Production. Records of the action taken shall be recorded in the Corrective Action Report (R/17-01).

Management Representative shall monitor achievements or non-achievements of objectives and targets through KPI Performance Reports. In case of non-achievement of objectives and targets, a corrective action shall be initiated by the respective HODs and the same shall be recorded in Corrective Action Report (R/17-01).

steps.heading: Non-compliance with documented consumer product management system

body.text: Non-compliance with documented management system shall be identified during internal audit. The concerned HOD shall identify the root cause of the nonconformities and shall initiate appropriate corrective action. Records of such action taken shall be recorded in the Internal Audit Nonconformity Report.

Noncompliance with documented management system shall also be identified during external audit. Analysis of root cause of the detected nonconformities and appropriate corrective action against those nonconformities shall be taken by the concerned prime responsible person. Root cause analysis and corrective action taken shall also be recorded.

steps.responsible: Concerned HOD; concerned prime responsible person

substeps.text: Corrective Action taken shall be appropriate to the magnitude of the problems. Corrective Action shall be reviewed through product hazard and risk assessment process prior to implementation.

As per organization’s policy, any corrective action plan relating to safety, legality or quality shall only be agreed by personnel who have defined responsibility and accountability for these areas of control. These personnel shall also be responsible for verifying that the corrective action plan has been completed satisfactorily. The name of concerned responsible and accountable person shall be mentioned in Corrective Action Report (R/17-01).
5 Why tools shall be used for assessing the root cause and necessary corrective action taken guidance.

All corrective actions shall be undertaken in a timely manner to prevent further occurrence of nonconformity. The target date of completion of corrective action shall be mentioned in Corrective Action Report (R/17-01).

Review of corrective actions shall be done to identify the effectiveness of implemented action. Revalidation of 1st review for corrective action after fixed interval as per the intensity of the problem shall also be monitored.
Any procedural changes or updating resulting from the corrective action shall be done through document control system.

Effectiveness of Corrective Action shall be reviewed by the Internal Auditors during internal audit. Corrective Actions taken as well as its effectiveness shall also be reviewed in the Management Review Meeting.

steps.heading: Actual and potential failure in product quality

body.text:
Actual failures in product quality can be detected during inspection and testing of product at relevant stage of product realization processes. They shall be reported in relevant QA reports. Nonconforming products, as detected from inspection and testing, shall be dealt as per method described in P-20, Procedure for Control of Nonconforming Product. Further, HOD- Quality Assurance along with HOD-Production shall investigate the nonconformities for determining the root cause and shall initiate appropriate corrective action. Result of investigation and corrective action taken shall be recorded in Corrective Action Report.

Potential failures in product quality may occur in case of violation of critical control point and/ or deviation of process control parameters. Violation of critical control point and/ or deviation of process control parameters shall be detected during monitoring of critical control points or during monitoring of process parameters. The same shall be reported in relevant reports. Monitoring data shall be analyzed by HOD-Quality Assurance along with HOD- Production and appropriate action (correction) shall be taken immediately to bring the process or system back into control. Further, HOD-Quality Assurance along with HOD- Production shall investigate the failures for determining the root cause and shall initiate appropriate corrective action. Result of investigation and corrective action taken shall be recorded in Corrective Action Report.

steps.heading: Failure in meeting legislative, environmental, OHS requirements

body.text: Noncompliance with legislative requirements shall be detected either during initial stages of product development or during periodic verification of legislative requirements. In case noncompliance is detected during initial stages of product development, effort shall be made to comply with the legislative requirements. Commitment to customer about executing the order shall not be given unless all the relevant legislative requirements are fulfilled. In case noncompliance is detected during periodic verification of legislative requirements, environmental and OHS related all relevant dispatches shall be stopped with immediate effect and effort shall be made to comply with the legislative requirements. Product dispatches shall resume only when all the relevant legislative requirements are fulfilled.

steps.heading: Detection of foreign body in the product

body.text:
Presence of glass, ceramic and brittle-plastic material shall be detected during physical verification of product. The same shall be reported in Incident Report (R/19-03) along with the location. All affected products shall be inspected in order to ensure product safety, legality and quality. Subsequently, HOD-Production shall initiate immediate action in order to mitigate the impact on product. The same shall be recorded in incident report itself.

All glass, ceramic and brittle-plastic breakages in the shop floor shall be reported in Incident Report (R/19-03). Affected products, if any, shall be segregated and inspected in order to ensure product safety, legality and quality. Subsequently, HOD-Production shall initiate immediate action in order to mitigate the impact on product. The same shall be recorded in incident report itself.

Further, HOD-Production shall investigate the incident of foreign body detection in the product for determining the root cause and shall initiate appropriate corrective action. Result of investigation and corrective action taken shall be recorded in Corrective Action Report.

As a preventive measures, specific work instructions shall be developed and displayed at suitable locations within the shop floor for handling of glass, ceramic and brittle-plastic breakages in raw material handling, preparation, processing, packing and storage areas.

All finished products shall be passed through metal detector. The same shall be recorded in Metal Detection Register (R/19-02). In case of any failure, as indicated by failure-alert, the affected product shall be segregated and inspected in order to ensure product safety, legality and quality. Subsequently, HOD-Production shall initiate immediate action in order to mitigate the impact on product. The same shall be recorded in metal detection register itself.

Further, HOD-Production shall investigate the incident of metal detection in the product for determining the root cause and shall initiate appropriate corrective action. Result of investigation and corrective action taken shall be recorded in Corrective Action Report.

The critical limits for detection, having due regard to the nature of the product, the location of the detector and any other factors influencing the sensitivity of the detector shall be defined and documented by HOD-QA.

HOD-QA shall also establish and implement procedure for operation and routine monitoring and testing of the metal detector (DS/19-01). In the event of the monitoring and testing procedure identifying any failure of the detector, HOD-Production shall initiate immediate action to mitigate the impact on product. These will include the isolation, quarantining, re- inspection through calibrated metal detector, recoded in R/19-02”, and safe disposal of all product since last acceptance test of the detector.

Incident of needle breakages shall be reported by production and the same shall be recorded in Needle Inventory and Replacement Record. Concerned maintenance personnel shall replace the broken needle with new one and shall collect the broken pieces of needle. The broken pieces of needle shall be pasted in Record of Broken Needle register.

steps.heading: Measures to Protect Third-Party Data from Unauthorized Access or Disclosure

body.text: Measures to Protect Third-Party Data from Unauthorized Access or Disclosure

Restricted Access Zones: Data storage areas, both physical (file rooms) and digital (data centers), are classified as Restricted Access Zones.

Employee Access ID: Access to restricted zones requires authorized employee ID badges. Only employees with authorized access may enter.

Visitor Protocols: Any external visitor must be accompanied by an authorized employee and sign in and out at security checkpoints.

User Permissions: Digital access to confidential data is managed through role-based access controls (RBAC). Access permissions are assigned based on job roles and strictly reviewed by the IT department.

Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA): All employees accessing sensitive data must use MFA to ensure secure login and minimize unauthorized access risk.

Audit Trails: System logs monitor data access, and audit trails are reviewed regularly to detect unauthorized access attempts.

Data Encryption: All sensitive data, including client information, is stored and transmitted in an encrypted format.

Regular Security Audits: The IT department conducts quarterly security audits to ensure data protection protocols are up-to-date and functioning as intended.

Employee Training: Employees receive training on data security policies, including how to identify phishing attempts and report unauthorized access.

Clear and Transparent Communication: Information is provided in a simple, easily understandable language, free from complex legal terminology to ensure clarity.

Retention Policy: Data is retained only as long as necessary to fulfill its purpose or meet legal and regulatory requirements. Regular reviews ensure data that is no longer needed is securely deleted.

blocks.text:
PURPOSE AND SCOPE
The purpose of this procedure is to have a system of controlling nonconforming products at every stage to ensure that product which does not conform to product requirements is identified and controlled to prevent its unintended use or delivery.
All category of products (Incoming, in process and Final Products) shall be within the scope of this procedure.

columns: Responsibility For dealing with NC Products

sections.title: Procedure for Control of Nonconforming Product (Doc. No.: P-24)

body.text:
The incoming raw materials, accessories, product-contact materials shall become nonconforming when a) the product does not conform with the specification decided by the organization and specified in the purchase order, b) there is presence of pest infestation.
The organization deals with nonconforming incoming products by returning the nonconforming product to the respective supplier and asking for its replenishment.
In case of nonconforming incoming products as revealed during inspection, the affected products shall be properly identified, segregated and stored in pre-defined location.
Supplier shall be informed about such nonconformity by HOD-Purchase. Supplier shall be asked to replace those nonconforming products. Record of such intimation and final disposition action shall be recorded in Nonconforming Product Report (R/15-01).

The in-process products shall become nonconforming when the product does not conform with the specification as specified in the job order file.
The organization deals with nonconforming in process products by –
taking suitable action (rework) to eliminate the detected nonconformity
considering in process products for rejection waste, if correction is not possible
In case nonconformity is detected at any stage during production process, Quality Assurance department shall inform the same to Production. Concerned Production personnel shall initiate necessary action (rework) to eliminate the detected nonconformities. After rework, the product is subjected to re-inspection.
In case rework is not possible, then the in-process product shall be stored in pre-defined location. This nonconforming in process product shall be disposed of as rejection waste. Record of nonconforming products as well as disposition action shall be reported in Nonconforming Product Report (R/15-01).

The finished product shall become nonconforming when the product does not conform with the specification as specified in the job order file.
The organization deals with nonconforming finished products by –
quarantine the nonconforming product batch for further disposal,
taking suitable action (rework) to eliminate the detected nonconformity,
considering products for rejection waste, if correction is not possible
In case of nonconforming finished products as revealed from the inspection, the affected nonconforming finished product shall be identified as “QC HOLD”.
Concerned Production or Packing personnel shall initiate necessary action (rework) to eliminate the detected nonconformities. After rework, the product is subjected to re- inspection.
In case rework is not possible, then the finished product shall be stored in pre-defined location. This nonconforming finished product shall be disposed of as rejection waste. Record of nonconforming products as well as disposition action shall be reported in Nonconforming Product Report (R/15-01).

Non-toxic or organic-based materials are preferred for their environmental benefits, aligning with Ganges Jute’s sustainability mission.

steps.heading: Reduction of Material Consumption through Process Optimization

body.text:
Optimization Initiatives: Production optimization to minimize resource usage reflects Ganges Jute’s dedication to responsible practices. This includes implementing energy- efficient technologies in machinery and reducing chemical and water use in processes.

Evidence of Recovery: Scrap materials are used for internal packaging or, if possible, donated for community initiatives, including educational programs for underprivileged children supported by Ganges Jute.
Documentation: All recovered materials are documented in the Recovered Materials Register (R/ENV-04) and are periodically reviewed for compliance.

steps.heading: Use of Eco-friendly or Bio-based Input Materials

body.text:
Procurement of Bio-based Materials: The procurement team prioritizes sourcing eco- friendly materials such as bio-based plastics, natural fibers, and biodegradable inputs.
Example: Where possible, Ganges Jute uses bio-based, sustainable materials like organic jute and natural dyes, supporting its mission for high-quality, environmentally responsible jute products.
Verification and Monitoring: Our agreement with suppliers of eco-friendly materials ensures they are assessed not only for material quality but also for ethical sourcing and sustainability practices, aligning with Ganges Jute's mission. (R/ENV-05).

steps.heading: Actions for Labeling, Storing, Handling, and Transporting Hazardous Substances

body.text:
Labeling: Each hazardous substance must be labeled per legal standards. Labels should include handling instructions and emergency contact information.
Storage: Hazardous substances are stored in designated, ventilated areas to prevent contamination. Storage locations have clear signage and spill containment systems in place.
Handling Protocols:
Personnel must undergo regular training on the handling of hazardous materials.
Only authorized personnel are allowed access to hazardous substance storage areas.
Ganges Jute prioritizes employee safety by providing continuous training on handling hazardous substances and offering immediate access to 24/7 medical support
Transportation: Hazardous substances are transported using certified carriers with appropriate safety certifications, including transport documentation (R/ENV-06).

blocks.text: Work Processes or Technologies Implemented to Mitigate Emissions of Dust and/or Particulate Matter

body.text: Ganges Jute has installed state-of-the-art dust collection and extraction systems to capture airborne dust generated during production processes.
Implementing water sprinkler systems throughout the facility helps to minimize dust dispersion in the air, particularly in high-traffic areas.
Filtration devices are employed on machinery to trap and remove particulate matter before it can enter the atmosphere.
Regular clean-up processes are enforced to minimize the accumulation of dust on surfaces, ensuring a clean and safe working environment.

Work Processes or Technologies Implemented to Mitigate Noise. Installation of noise control walls, such as greenbelt barriers and sound barrier blankets, reduces the transmission of noise to surrounding areas.
Equipment generating high noise levels is housed within acoustic enclosures to contain and minimize noise emissions.
Mufflers and silencers are used on exhaust air systems and pneumatic equipment to reduce noise levels during operation.
Areas with high noise generation are insulated to contain sound and prevent leakage into the environment.
Work Processes or Technologies Implemented to Mitigate Odor. Odorous materials are stored in isolated areas to prevent the release of smells into the surrounding environment.
Ventilation systems are designed to manage and direct odors away from workspaces and external areas, ensuring that emissions do not adversely affect air quality.
Regular monitoring of odor emissions is conducted to assess the effectiveness of implemented controls.

4.4 Company-Specific Actions to Avoid Road Congestion. Ganges Jute has implemented traffic management plans to avoid congestion near facility entry and exit points. This includes scheduling large vehicle arrivals and departures during off-peak hours.
Designated routes for delivery and transport vehicles are communicated to drivers to avoid high-traffic roads near the facility.
Staggered work shifts are introduced to reduce the number of vehicles entering and exiting the premises simultaneously, reducing road congestion and improving traffic flow.
Employees are encouraged to participate in carpooling programs, reducing vehicle count on surrounding roads and minimizing traffic impact.

Closed-Circuit System to Reduce Sulfur Emissions. The facility has installed a closed-circuit sulfur absorption system for textile manufacturing processes, particularly viscose production, to capture and contain sulfur emissions. All sulfur-generating processes are conducted within enclosed areas to prevent sulfur dispersion into the atmosphere.

Specialized sulfur recovery units are installed to capture sulfur emissions. The recovered sulfur is then recycled back into the process or safely stored for disposal, significantly reducing sulfur emissions.

Quarterly Maintenance Checks: The Maintenance Team conducts quarterly inspections of the closed-circuit sulfur recovery system to ensure it is functioning efficiently. Emission Reports: Monthly sulfur emission levels are documented and submitted to the EHS Manager for review, ensuring emissions remain within permissible limits.

In the event of a significant emission event (e.g., excessive dust release, noise complaints, or odor incidents), the following steps will be taken: Immediate Assessment: The EHS Manager will conduct a rapid assessment to identify the source and extent of the emission. Containment Measures: Appropriate containment measures will be implemented to limit the spread of emissions. Notification Protocol: Relevant stakeholders, including local authorities and affected community members, will be notified as per established protocols. Corrective Actions: Identify and implement corrective actions to prevent recurrence.

steps.heading: Adoption of Waterless or Water-Saving Dyeing Methods

body.text: Water-Efficient Dyeing Technologies:

substeps.text: Ganges Jute uses low-liquor dyeing techniques that reduce water use in traditional dyeing by 40-50%, improving water efficiency.
Waterless Dyeing Technologies: Supercritical CO₂ dyeing is used for specific products, allowing dye to be transferred without water, saving up to 95% of water normally required in dyeing.

body.text: Evidence of Implementation:

substeps.text: Operational Pilot Programs: Waterless dyeing methods, such as supercritical CO₂ technology, are implemented in select dyeing units, with plans for future expansion based on performance results.

body.text: Monitoring and Reporting:

steps.heading: Technologies or Practices to Recycle or Reuse Water

body.text: Closed-Loop Water Recycling Systems:

substeps.text: Closed-loop systems capture wastewater from dyeing, washing, and rinsing processes, treat it, and recirculate it for further use, reducing water intake by up to 70-80%.
Reuse in Facility Operations: Reclaimed water is used for production processes, cooling systems, and irrigation, lowering the facility's water footprint and wastewater discharge.

body.text: Operational Processes for Reclaimed Water:

substeps.text: Filtration and Treatment: Reclaimed water undergoes a multi-step filtration and treatment process to meet quality standards before reuse.
Dedicated Reuse Points: Key areas in the facility, such as cooling systems and production support, use reclaimed water, minimizing fresh water dependency.

body.text: Documentation and Maintenance:

substeps.text: Recycling Log (GJ-R/WC-01): Daily logs capture the volume of water reclaimed and reused, reviewed monthly.
System Inspection: Closed-loop systems are inspected quarterly to ensure functionality and water quality.

body.text: Rainwater Capture and Storage:

substeps.text: Ganges Jute has installed rooftop and surface runoff rainwater harvesting systems, designed to capture rainwater from building surfaces and surrounding areas.
Storage Capacity: The system includes a pond with a storage capacity of 227,000 Liters, allowing for sustainable water use in non-potable applications.

body.text: Utilization and Maintenance:

substeps.text: Non-Potable Applications: Collected rainwater is used for factory cleaning, fire suppression systems, and irrigation.
Regular Maintenance: Monthly cleaning and inspection of gutters, pipes, and tanks ensure system efficiency, and annual water treatment ensures water quality.

body.text: Monitoring and Impact Reporting:

substeps.text: Rainwater Usage Report (GJ-R/WC-02): Monthly reports detail the amount of rainwater captured and utilized, with year-over-year comparisons to track water savings.
Environmental Impact Assessment: Rainwater harvesting has reduced groundwater use by 30%, contributing to local water conservation efforts.

sops.title: Procedure for Third-Party Due Diligence on ESG

blocks.text: The purpose of this procedure is to establish a comprehensive, structured, and risk-based due diligence framework for evaluating and managing third parties from an Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) perspective.
This procedure aims to:

Integrate ESG principles into procurement and supply chain decisions
Identify, assess, and mitigate ESG-related risks associated with third parties
Prevent environmental violations, unethical practices, and human rights abuses
Ensure responsible sourcing and sustainable procurement practices
Safeguard the organization from legal, financial, operational, and reputational risks
Promote continuous improvement and alignment with global sustainability expectations
This procedure is designed to align with international best practices, including:

ESG frameworks and responsible sourcing standards
Applicable environmental and labor regulations
Internal policies on ethics, environment, and human rights
This procedure applies to all third parties engaged directly or indirectly by Ganges Jute Pvt. Ltd. across all operations, including:

Raw material suppliers (e.g., raw jute, chemicals, oils)
Packaging and auxiliary material vendors
Contractors and subcontractors
Logistics and transport service providers

Maintenance and service providers
It covers the entire lifecycle of third-party engagement, including:

responsibilities: Develop and maintain ESG due diligence framework, conduct risk assessments, review high-risk cases, and ensure regulatory compliance.

body.text: The organization shall adopt a risk-based approach to ensure that due diligence efforts are proportional to the level of ESG risk associated with each third party.

Social risks (labor intensity, worker conditions)

Risk Categorization:

Low Risk: Minimal ESG exposure, low operational impact
Medium Risk: Moderate ESG risks requiring monitoring
High Risk: Significant ESG exposure requiring enhanced due diligence
Before onboarding, all third parties shall undergo a structured ESG screening process.
